title: Organizer evaluation scenario
description: One hand-authored, fully synthetic week. It generates every intake asset (API items, rendered screenshots) and carries every gold label (item->events, item->persons, facts with supersession, status-line checkpoints). Gold fields (events, persons, facts, checkpoints, tags) are never sent to the organizer; tools/to_items.py strips them.

split.description: dev may be tuned on; holdout is scored separately and never tuned on.

synthetic.description: Guard: run_eval.py refuses to send a scenario that is not marked synthetic.

home_rubric.description: How checkpoint home grades (0-3) were assigned. Grades come from the scenario's own dates and stakes, never from model outputs; holdout grades are frozen before any holdout run is scored.

owner_person_id.description: The Mac's user. Excluded from person-linking metrics.

actions.description: Optional act-stage log: exports of one event as plain text to Claude/Codex/a person, with the item that brought the result back. Gold only; never sent.

demo_threads.description: Optional demo storylines: which items to replay for each.

generation.description: Optional provenance of a generated scenario (plan seed, generator tools, models, nodes, throughput). Not used for scoring and never sent to the organizer.

person_questions.description: Optional gold for person-identity questions: surfaces that must be asked (two candidates) or merged (recognition errors, nicknames).

source.description: Optional path of the scenario bible the plan was derived from.

aliases.description: Other surface names used for this person in other sources (chat nicknames, how people address them, the Mac's voice label).

voice.description: How the Mac's on-device voice pipeline sees this person, or null (or absent) if they never speak in an audio item. Audio and voiceprints never leave the Mac; only mac_person_id and the user's label travel with a transcript.

user_label.description: Name the user gave this voice on the Mac; null = recognised but not yet named.

tts_hint.description: Optional hint for synthesising audio for this person.

kind.description: main = a real matter; decoy = a real but separate matter built to look like decoy_of; noise = a label that marks items as belonging to no event (the scorer drops noise-kind labels from gold).

now.description: Optional: where the matter stands at the end of the scenario (one line).

related.description: Other events this one links to (not the same matter).

lookalike_of.description: Events built to look like this one but that are separate matters.

anchor.description: The formal object the matter is about (contract, PO, document).

person_id.description: Gold speaker (a people[].person_id). to_items.py replaces it with that person's mac_person_id.

sender.description: Name as shown in the chat app (often an alias).

style.description: generic_im (default) = chat screen (messages); generic_table = spreadsheet/dashboard table (columns, rows); generic_terminal = terminal window (lines); generic_card = document, receipt, notice, alert, ticket, SMS, calendar or offer card (fields as {label, value} objects or [label, value] pairs); generic_design = design mock with review notes (blocks, annotations); generic_doc = a scanned page (paragraphs); board = dashboard (title, kpis, rows, chart); doc/table = document page (title, rows, lines); whiteboard (lines); photo = drawn stand-in scene with annotation lines. All drawn in neutral generic styles by tools/render_screenshots.py; none imitates a real app.

self_sender.description: Sender name drawn on the right as the Mac user's own bubbles.

ocr_text.description: Gold: the text a reader can see in the image.

ref.description: Short human handle, e.g. d3-02. Also names the rendered PNG.

kind.description: Same values as the organizer API ItemKind.

source_app.description: e.g. 微信, 腾讯会议, 线下, Claude, Codex, ChatGPT, Finder, 淘宝.

persons.description: Gold: people who speak, send, are addressed or are named in the item (implicit references like '那个师傅' are not labelled).

events.description: Gold multi-label item->events; empty = noise that should belong to no event. Order follows the order the matters appear in the item.

tags.description: Analysis tags: agent_result, noise, injection, multi_label, decoy_bridge.

segments.description: Voice segments of a meeting, or for a text item covering several matters its gold segments [{event_id, quote}] (never mixed in one item).

event_segments.description: Gold segments of a multi-matter item (also one that has voice segments): which verbatim span belongs to which event; event_id null = unrelated aside.

file.description: Optional original file the user dropped in (any format), relative to the scenario directory. to_items.py sends its bytes (file_b64, filename, mime_type); text, if present, is the caption the user typed with it.

file_truth.description: Gold: ground-truth JSON of file (text, key fields, QA), relative to the scenario directory. Never sent.

file_text.description: Gold: the file's readable content (copied from file_truth) so score.py can ground claims in it. Never sent (to_items.py --file-text gold sends it as an oracle reading).

asset.description: Optional rendered file (PNG/PDF) relative to the scenario directory.

format.description: Optional: the intake/export format the item imitates, e.g. tencent_transcript, feishu_transcript, zoom_transcript, zoom_vtt, zoom_txt, chat_paste, phone_ime, mac_dictation, email, claude_result, codex_result, doc_text, screenshot, pdf, calendar_text. Not sent to the organizer.

input_mode.description: Optional: phone keyboard typed or voice input, or Mac Fn dictation.

content_time.description: Optional: when the content itself happened, if earlier than t (a pasted old chat, a late transcript export, a PDF dragged in days later).

event_spans.description: Optional segment-level gold for multi-matter items: which piece of the item is about which event.

facts_introduced.description: Facts whose valid_from is this item (derived).

followup_of.description: An earlier item this one continues, days later, without naming the matter.

split_of.description: First half of the same chat, pasted earlier.

distractor_of.description: The look-alike event this item is built to be confused with.

expected_ask.description: A question the organizer may reasonably ask here, with the gold answer.

generator.description: Provenance of generated text (model, node, attempts, checks).

source.description: Where the item came from (finer than kind/source_app).

imported_at.description: When the user brought the item in, if later than t (late meeting exports).

facts.description: Gold: which arc facts this item conveys and how.

should_ask.description: Gold: a genuine ambiguity the organizer should ask about once.

ground_truth_text.description: All text drawn in a screenshot.

matter_segments.description: Gold, multi-matter items: for each event, a verbatim quote of the part of the item that is about it.

fact_refs.description: Gold: facts the item states. new = first evidence; repeat = restated while still valid; stale = restated after it was superseded (must not pull the status back).

person_mentions.description: Gold: the surface form each person has in this item (aliases collide across people).

sensitive.description: Gold: sensitive categories in the item (薪酬, 绩效, 健康 ...).

reading.description: Gold: the standard reading of an image or PDF (what a correct reader extracts).

keys.description: All keys must appear in the normalised status line; '|' separates alternatives inside one key. Normalisation: NFKC, lower case, no spaces/commas, numbers (1.5万=15000=一万五), dates (9/28=9月28号=9月28日).

valid_from.description: item_id at which the fact becomes true (its evidence).

superseded_by.description: fact_id that replaces this one; from that fact's valid_from on, mentioning this one without the replacement counts as stale.

state.description: Progress state at valid_from. A planned fact matched in a clause that claims completion scores as plan_as_done, not as recall.

date.description: Resolved date of a planned action (from the evidence item's capture time).

after_item_id.description: Snapshot is taken after this item (in time order) has been ingested and processed.

expected.description: event_id -> fact_ids that event's one status line should state at this checkpoint.

home.description: Expected home-screen importance at this checkpoint (see home_rubric). Every non-noise gold event with items at or before after_item_id is graded; noise cards are implicitly 0.

reference_order.description: Optional: an author-written reference order of the top of the home screen (ties in grades broken by the scenario's own story).

gold_segment.description: Segment-level truth: a verbatim quote from the item text (as sent) and the event that part belongs to. Scored by score.py segment Link F1.

event_id.description: The event this part is about; null = an unrelated aside.

quote.description: Verbatim piece of the item that is about this event.

target.description: Claude, Codex, 自己, or a person_id.
